summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten: Off-World Artifacts Mission Archive is an interactive, web-based educational archive designed to provide context for decommissioned NASA hardware in lunar, Martian and deep space environments. The platform is a responsive single page application, created with semantic HTML5, modular CSS3 and asynchronous JavaScript, and combines verified mission telemetry with accessible scientific storytelling.

The archive contains records of thirteen historically important spacecraft and surface instruments, including Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, ALSEP stations, Surveyor landers, Martian explorers (Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking 1 and 2, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity), and deep-space probes (Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 and 11). Every dossier combines authentic NASA archival imagery, planetary coordinates, technical specifications and subsystem analyses with narrative profiles and an interactive AI assistant, Commander Cosmo, to facilitate real-time student inquiry.

The platform combines the technical documentation of spacecraft with pedagogical storytelling, turning inactive spacecraft into educational stories. Abandoned but not Forgotten presents decommissioned off-world equipment through a filterable registry, high resolution lightbox galleries and clear conceptual analogies to encourage scientific literacy in future generations of scientists and engineers.
details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten — Off-World Artifacts Mission Archive is an interactive web-based educational archive and mission-control interface for documenting decommissioned NASA hardware in the lunar, Martian and deep space environments. The site is a responsive single page application (SPA) that organizes thirteen significant artifacts that are historically relevant to space exploration, such as the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles, ALSEP scientific stations, Surveyor landers, Martian rovers and landers (Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking 1 and 2, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity), and deep space probes (Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10, and Pioneer 11), into a categorized, real-time searchable registry.

Artifacts are selected and a multi-layered technical dossier is dynamically generated that shows verified operational telemetry, planetary coordinates, engineering specifications, subsystem breakdowns, full screen lightbox inspection of archival NASA photographs, and a narrative profile that is accessible. Also, the platform includes Commander Cosmo, an embedded conversational AI assistant, built with the Cohere API (with a built-in local fallback system), that lets students ask real-time questions about each mission's history and engineering.

The Project has a number of benefits, including:

Centralized Accessibility: Gathers all mission logs, coordinate references, engineering specifications and public domain NASA imagery in one easy-to-use, installation-free, software-free central location.

Inquiry Based Learning: Integrates structured technical information with interactive subsystem tabs, search filtering, and real-time AI Q&A to promote active learning over passive reading.

Offline & Network Resilience: Lightweight client side architecture and local conversational fallback logic means that core educational content will continue to work even if the internet connection is unstable.

Intended Impact

The project seeks to change the perception of the decommissioned space hardware from "abandoned space debris" to "permanent monuments of human curiosity, engineering resilience and scientific discovery. The archive's combination of high-quality aerospace information and accessible storytelling and conceptual analogies makes the study of aerospace science accessible to a wide audience, and promotes scientific literacy and the next generation of aerospace engineers, planetary scientists, and explorers.

The tools, coding languages, hardware and software used are described .Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used are described.

Languages & Web Standards: Semantic HTML5, modular CSS3 (with CSS Grid, Flexbox, custom properties and responsive media queries), and vanilla ES6+ JavaScript.

APIs & Libraries: Cohere Chat API (command-r-plus) for the Commander Cosmo conversational assistant, Google Fonts (Space Grotesk and DM Mono), and NASA Open Image and Video Library assets.

Software & Development Environment: Visual Studio Code (Live Server for local testing and debugging), and modern web browsers for cross device rendering verification. Canva for creating a presentation. VS code AI for the help of creating the project

Creativity & Innovation

This project is not a traditional encyclopedia or slide show, but a full-fledged Mission Control HUD (Heads-Up Display) complete with real-time status indicators, telemetry grids, engineering schematics, and more. This is also done through a two-layered communication approach: formal engineering reports are paired with age-appropriate, engaging stories, accompanied by an in-character astronaut AI companion.

The factors taken into account by our team are listed below .Our team considers the following factors:

Simplicity vs. Scientific Rigor: We were conscious of the need to balance accurate NASA mission telemetry and planetary coordinates with accessible vocabulary so that younger students could understand complex engineering concepts without oversimplifying the science.

Data Attribution & Reliability: Clear and explicit attribution of NASA archival sources, clear and transparent coordinate reference frame for exact surface locations when the same is not verified, and graceful failure for visual schematics and AI connectivity.
